title: Shipline: weekly cut, RC gating, and automated changelog pipeline
creator: Jordan Keane
description:
Goal: Create a reproducible weekly release pipeline ("shipline") that produces nightly/weeky build artifacts, marks candidate releases as RC tags, enforces rollout gates for LTS vs stable channels, and publishes a consumer-friendly changelog automatically to the Docs and Console UI.

Background: We currently perform manual steps to cut weekly builds and RC tags. Release notes are curated by hand which delays release communication and introduces human error in LTS backports. This ticket implements an automated, audit-friendly pipeline that integrates with existing upgrade tooling and rollout gates.

Success criteria / Acceptance:
- Every weekly cut produces a semver tag and an RC tag (e.g., v1.19.3-rc.20260312) in GitHub with an associated release artifact in the artifacts bucket.
- Automated changelog generated from merged PRs and linked JIRA/Linear issues, published to Confluence and surfaced in Console release notes.
- Rollout gate enforcement: canary -> regional ramp -> global based on telemetry and regression checks; LTS channel selection must be a protected path requiring 2 approvers.
- Upgrade tool (upgradectl) can compute a safe upgrade plan between any two versions produced by the pipeline.
- Rollback playbook executable via the console with one-click revert to previous stable tag.

Proposed design summary:
1) Tagging: Add a GitHub Action that runs on schedule (weekly + on-demand). It builds artifacts, computes semver bump rules (patch by default; major/minor via release notes field), then creates both a release tag and an RC tag (rc.<YYYYMMDD> suffix). RC tags are temporary and move to stable after gating.
2) Changelog: Use conventional commits + PR metadata to generate changelog. Rules to include: PRs with label "release-note:skip" are excluded; PRs must reference Linear keys to be included. Generated changelog is stored as markdown and pushed to Confluence via API and to the Console release notes service.
3) Rollout gates: Implement an orchestrator service that reads health metrics (latency, error-rate, infra saturation) from Observability and evaluates gating rules (thresholds configurable per release). If gate fails, pipeline halts and notifies on-call.
4) LTS selection: LTS channel promotion requires pipeline annotation "promote-to-lts" and manual approval by two engineers (release lead + security). The pipeline enforces RBAC for LTS promotions.
5) Upgrade tooling integration: upgradectl will be extended to read release metadata (artifact checksum, migration notes, dependencies) to produce an automated upgrade checklist.
6) Release notes automation: Generated notes should include component-level regressions, upgrade steps, known issues, and links to failing e2e tests.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: GH Action for tagging and artifact publishing (Maya).
- Week 2: Changelog generator + Confluence/Console publishing (Jordan + Docs).
- Week 3: Gate evaluator service + observability hooks (SRE).
- Week 4: LTS promotion workflow + RBAC enforcement + upgradectl integration (release team).

Rollout & monitoring:
- Initial rollout to canary org only. If canary metrics stable for 48h, auto-ramp to 25% customer traffic, then to 100% after 7 days with no regressions.
- Alerting: Gate failures create a P1 in oncall channel and create a Linear ticket prefixed with REL- for tracking.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Automating LTS promotions reduces manual oversight—mitigated by requiring two approvers and an audit log.
- Changelog automation may miss context-rich notes; Docs will have an "augment" step for release leads to add narrative before promotion to LTS.
- Tight coupling with Observability APIs requires clear SLAs; fallback is manual gating via release lead.

Notes & links:
- Prototype GH Action: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-actions/pull/124 (PR-124)
- Draft Confluence page (design + audit): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Shipline+Design
- Upgrade tooling prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/upgradectl (branch: release-infra-shipline)

Acceptance test checklist:
- [ ] GitHub tag + artifact exists for a scheduled cut
- [ ] Changelog page created and linked to PRs
- [ ] Gate evaluator correctly blocks a simulated regression
- [ ] LTS promotion requires approvals and leaves an audit record
- [ ] upgradectl computes plan for two semantic versions

Next steps: Kick off PR for GH Action and draft the Confluence changelog template. Coordinate with Docs and SRE for metrics wiring.
